annotation.reasoning_summary: Polygon footprints represent housing association-owned buildings/complexes, not a full tessellation. The decisive rule is object: discrete managed property parcels with numeric attributes, so not AmountDS.
Point features represent identifiable archaeological cesspits and finds at addresses; this is a set of discrete objects, not measurements or events.
Point features mark discrete archaeological finds/locations with object codes and captions; this is best treated as identifiable objects rather than measures or events.
Polygons mark discrete archaeological sites/vindplaatsen with names, addresses, and descriptions, so the layer represents identifiable bounded objects rather than a tessellation, coverage, or patch.
Polygons mark selected park/area zones with BBQ restrictions, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive entity rule is patch: bounded phenomenon areas with categorical BBQ status.
Polygon layer of named conservation areas/protected city and village views; these are discrete bounded heritage objects, not a full tessellation or reporting unit.
Point layer of wild bee observations with year attributes; the decisive rule is event/occurrence over time at point locations, not point objects or amounts.
Point features represent honey bee locations/apiaries as distinct countable objects; the numeric hive/colony fields are attributes, not the main mapped phenomenon.

Polygon regions classify soil-quality categories by area (zones like Zone 1/2, saneringsgebied, infrastructuur) rather than reporting units; this is a full-area thematic coverage, not a tessellation of administrative units or discrete objects.
Point layer of individual trees; each point is a distinct real-world object with attributes like species, planting year, and owner, so this is ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual trees with identifiers, species, height, owner, and manager attributes; this is a discrete object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent individual trees, a countable real-world object layer. Numeric fields like boomnummer, plantjaar, and radius are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features represent individual trees with species, year planted, owner/manager, and tree type attributes; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark distinct compost collection locations/initiatives (street-name based sites) with descriptive attributes; this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Polygon areas named as camera zones; they are discrete bounded areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units, so PatchDS with PlainVectorRegion.

Point features represent individual trees (Canadian poplars) with IDs, species, district, and action/status attributes; this is a set of identifiable real-world objects, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent individual crowd-monitoring sensors/cameras (distinct assets), so this is PointDS with ObjectDS rather than a measurement or amount layer.

Polygon areas mark selected cultural-historical exploration zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units. They are bounded thematic patches describing investigation areas, so PlainVectorRegion + PatchDS.
Point features mark knotweed occurrences/records, not a measurement field; numeric area is just an attribute. Classified as point objects (ObjectDS) using the point/object rule.
Point features mark discrete ecopassage bottleneck objects/locations (routes, bridges, passages) rather than measurements or events; classified as ObjectDS by the point-object rule.

Polygon/MultiPolygon areas are discrete selected wind-energy potential zones, not a full tessellation. The decisive entity rule is patch: bounded phenomenon areas with numeric capacity/yield attributes, but the main mapped feature is the potential area itself rather than the numbers.
Point features represent distinct election polling locations (Stemlocatie) with vote statistics as attributes, so the decisive rule is object points, not amount or measures.
Point layer of oak processionary caterpillar nests tied to individual trees (Boom_ID); the main phenomenon is discrete objects with status/date attributes, not a measurement or amount.
Polygon areas form an area-wide regulatory zoning/tessellation for pedicab permissions and restrictions, so the geometry is a vector tessellation and the entity is coverage of thematic area classes.
Points represent discrete pedicab/horse-carriage stand locations (standplaatsen), so this is a point object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features represent individual non-residential buildings/addresses with function labels; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Polygon areas classify the whole map into functional land-use mix categories (WON/VZN/WRK) rather than reporting units or discrete objects; this fits a full-area thematic coverage layer.
Neighborhood polygons form an area partition of Amsterdam (tessellation). They are reporting/administrative units with codes and area attributes, so LatticeDS.

Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so this is a tessellation. The layer represents reporting/administrative units (buurtcombinaties) with area attributes, which fits LatticeDS.

Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so the geometry is VectorTessellation. The layer is an administrative/reporting unit layer (buurten/neighborhoods) with codes and area attributes, so it is LatticeDS.

Neighborhood polygons form a near-complete partition of Amsterdam, so the geometry is a tessellation. The features are reporting/statistical units (buurten) with area attributes, so the entity is LatticeDS.
City districts are administrative reporting units that partition Amsterdam, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS.

City districts are administrative/reporting units that partition Amsterdam into near-complete area units, so the geometry is a tessellation and the entity is LatticeDS; the area field is just an attribute.
Polygon layer of named Amsterdam areas that together form the city’s area division; this is a reporting/administrative unit tessellation, so VectorTessellation + LatticeDS.

The layer shows Amsterdam areas that partition the city into reporting/administrative units (22 gebieden excl. water), so it is a tessellation. The decisive entity rule is reporting unit/statistical area, even though Opp_m2 is a numeric attribute.

These are named practice areas covering the city in polygon form, functioning as reporting/administrative units rather than discrete objects; the area field is an attribute, so the decisive rule is tessellation plus reporting unit.
The layer is a set of named practice areas that partition Amsterdam into near-complete region units; the area field is just an attribute. Decisive rules: tessellation and reporting-unit lattice.
Polygons are noise contour zones around industrial areas, not a full tessellation of reporting units. The decisive rule is contour/band classification from the 50DB noise zones.
Polygon bands labeled with dB ranges indicate contour/interval zones rather than a full tessellation or objects; decisive rule: contour-like value classes.

Polygons represent noise contour bands (dB classes), not a tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is contour/isoline-like value intervals, with the numeric KLASSE/SELECTIE indicating banded noise levels.
Polygonal noise contour bands with dB classes indicate contour/isoline zones, not a full tessellation or object layer.

Point features are polling stations/stemlocaties with election results attached; the layer represents discrete facilities/objects, not measurements or events. Geometry is PointDS and the decisive entity rule is ObjectDS for identifiable places with attributes.
Point features mark individual green-roof locations/projects (addresses, roof type, photos), so this is an object layer; numeric area/year fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.

Polygon land-use classification layer; polygons are discrete land-use areas within a thematic coverage rather than a reporting tessellation. Entity is CoverageDS because the map shows exhaustive area-wide land-use classes (e.g., traffic, residential, water, nature).
Point features mark identifiable historical buildings and related facilities, not measurements or events; numeric fields are dates/attributes, so the decisive rule is object points.

Polygon regions are discrete bounded municipal areas rather than a full tessellation. The decisive rule is object/area representation: the layer maps identifiable city/municipality polygons, with GEMEENTE_ID as an identifier, not a main amount or coverage field.
Polygon areas mark selected dog off-leash/restricted zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units; this fits bounded phenomenon patches. The decisive rule is PatchDS for special zones.
Polygon layer of named green-space sites (parks, cemeteries, corridors, etc.) with area attributes; these are discrete managed objects, not a full tessellation or numeric field.
Point features represent individual private elm trees (a countable real-world object); numeric/categorical fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features represent identifiable housing projects/buildings for youth and students; the numeric Aantal_woningen is an attribute, not the main mapped phenomenon, so ObjectDS fits best.
Point layer of individual chestnut trees; each point represents a distinct tree object, with damage status as an attribute rather than the main mapped quantity.
Point features with numeric groundwater/ground-level attributes; this is a point measurement layer rather than objects or amounts.
Polygon areas show flood-related zones with probability/depth classes; they are selected phenomenon patches rather than a full reporting tessellation or object layer.
Point layer of market locations; each point is a distinct real-world market object, not a measurement or event. Decision used: point geometry + object/facility classification.
Point geometries mark identifiable named green monuments/parks and related heritage sites; the numeric monument IDs and dates are attributes, not the main phenomenon.
Point features represent individual monumental trees; this is a discrete object layer, not measurements or events.
Point features represent identifiable monuments/buildings/assets, so the decisive rule is object points; the numeric monument number is just an attribute, not the main phenomenon.

Point features marking individual quay wall plant occurrences/species locations; the main phenomenon is identifiable biological objects, not measurements. Numeric counts are ancillary attributes, so ObjectDS fits better than AmountDS.

MultiPolygon units form a near-complete tessellation of Amsterdam reporting areas (CodeW), and the layer maps NO2 concentrations over time; by the reporting-unit and amount rules this is Lattice-like geometry with AmountDS.
Point layer of NO2 measurement locations; the main phenomenon is sampled air-quality measurement at points, so PointDS + PointMeasuresDS.
Polygon areas are discrete bounded zones, not a full tessellation; the layer maps selected gulch/area patches with a category field, so PatchDS is the best fit.
Point soundings/boreholes sample subsurface conditions at locations; the decisive rule is point measurement of a continuous geological phenomenon, not point objects or amounts.

Polygon layer of named development neighbourhoods; these are discrete bounded areas and the set is intended as a neighborhood partition, so Geometry is VectorTessellation. The features represent identifiable named areas/projects rather than a full-area thematic field or reporting units, so Entity is ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual public toilet locations/facilities; numeric price and opening details are attributes, so this is an object layer rather than amount or event.

Polygon layer of Amsterdam neighbourhoods/bounded zones used for overnight policy rules; these regions do not appear to be full thematic coverage or reporting units, so they fit a bounded patch/zone classification.
Polygons are discrete zone areas for parking-standard categories, not a full tessellation of reporting units. The decisive rule is coverage: an area-wide thematic classification by category (A/B/C).
Polygon footprints of named parks and green spaces; these are discrete bounded objects, not a full tessellation or amount layer. Numeric area is just an attribute, so ObjectDS.

Postcode4-buurten are postcode area polygons that partition Amsterdam, so geometry is a tessellation. They are reporting/statistical units identified by postcode, with area as an attribute, so entity is LatticeDS.
Polygon postcode areas are reporting/statistical units that partition Amsterdam; the key rule is tessellation plus reporting-unit classification, not the numeric area attribute.
Postal code polygons form a near-complete area partition, and the decisive rule is reporting/statistical units (postcode6/Buurtcode) rather than objects or amounts.
LineString features form a transport/infrastructure network; title and attributes (roads, routes, speed, tram/bus/auto classes) indicate connected route system, so LineDS + NetworkDS.

Polygons represent discrete pedestrian network zones/areas like parks and squares, not a full tessellation or reporting unit. The decisive rule is object-like bounded regions rather than coverage or patch classification.
Point features naming specific locations/masts; this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark privacy-related research/analysis items (e.g., investigations and pilot analyses), so the decisive rule is point-based event/occurrence mapping rather than objects or amounts.
Point locations mark named scan/measurement sites for the car fleet scan; these are identifiable real-world locations with addresses, so PointDS + ObjectDS.
Point layer of polling locations/stemlocaties for the 2019 provincial elections; the features are distinct voting places/objects with numeric vote attributes, so this is ObjectDS, not AmountDS.

Polygon areas are selected drainage-relevant zones, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The key meaning is where drainage is possible or not, so this fits a bounded phenomenon patch rather than coverage or lattice.
Polygons are discrete hydro units, not a full tessellation or reporting grid. The layer represents selected bounded Rainproof solution/target areas, so PatchDS is the best fit.
Polygon areas mark rainproof bottleneck zones/affected areas, not a full tessellation or reporting units. The decisive rule is patch: selected bounded phenomenon areas with urgency attributes.
Discrete polygon features marking named sewerage locations/projects, not a full tessellation or coverage; classify as identifiable objects (object rule).
Point features representing identifiable religious buildings/addresses, so geometry is PointDS and the main phenomenon is discrete real-world objects (religious sites), not measurements or events.
LineString features describe sidewalk segments along streets, so the layer is a connected route/infrastructure network; width and obstacle attributes are secondary, not the main phenomenon.
LineString features describe mopeds/roads routing on specific street segments, so this is a connected transport network layer rather than objects or amounts.
Point layer of identifiable public sports/playground facilities; the point locations represent distinct objects, and the numeric Oppervlak is just an attribute, not the main mapped phenomenon.
Point locations of city farming sites; each feature is a distinct real-world object/place (garden, farm, nursery), so ObjectDS with PointDS geometry.

Polygon features represent discrete city farming sites/parks with names, addresses, and websites, so this is an object layer rather than a tessellation or patch. The decisive rule is identifiable bounded objects.
Point features represent identifiable city-pilot initiatives/activities at locations; the year is just an attribute, so this is an object layer on points rather than an amount or event layer.
LineString layer of major streets; the decisive rule is network because it represents a connected street/route system, not numeric amounts.
Line geometries showing district heating/cooling transport infrastructure; decisive rule is network/route system, with status/type as attributes.
Polygon features show selected district heating/cooling areas by network type and status; they are bounded project zones, not a tessellation or reporting units, so PatchDS.

Polygon areas show selected strategic housing-plan zones rather than a full tessellation; they are bounded development/vision areas with attributes like project name and max housing count, so PatchDS fits better than AmountDS or ObjectDS.
Point features represent distinct local farming businesses/venues with names and addresses, so this is an object layer based on points, not a measurement or event layer.
LineString features represent tram and metro route lines; the decisive rule is network/route system, not the categorical line attributes.
LineString features represent tram and metro routes; this is a transport network, so use LineDS + NetworkDS.
Point features represent discrete tram stops and metro stations; the numeric radius and line fields are attributes, not the main phenomenon, so this is a point object layer.
Point geometry with named tram stops and metro stations; the layer represents discrete transport facilities (object) rather than measurements or events.
Point features represent distinct traffic light locations/controlled intersections, so this is a point object layer. Numeric fields are just attributes (IDs and dates), not the main phenomenon.
Line network of road links with traffic forecast volumes; geometry is lines and the main phenomenon is numeric traffic amount, so AmountDS with LineDS.
Point layer of election polling/stem locations; each point is a distinct voting place with vote-count attributes, so the decisive rule is object points rather than amount or event.
Point features represent individual trees with IDs, species, planting year, and size classes; this is an object layer, not a point-measures or amount map.
Point features represent distinct traffic information system devices (cameras/displays/signs) with identifiers and locations, so this is a point object layer, not an amount or measurement layer.

Point features represent distinct traffic information system installations (BFA devices/pollers) with IDs, type, location, and management attributes, so this is an object layer, not a measurement or event layer.
Point features mark discrete breeding bird nesting locations/addresses; numeric year fields are attributes of those object locations, so use PointDS + ObjectDS.
Point features represent individual benches in Vondelpark, a set of identifiable real-world objects. Numeric fields like rotation are just attributes, so this is ObjectDS rather than AmountDS.
LineString street segments for walkability; this is a connected route/street system, so NetworkDS. The numeric straatvaknummer is just an identifier, not the main phenomenon.
Point features mark individual wall-art works at specific addresses, so this is a point object layer rather than measurements or events.
Polygon areas classify the city into welstand niveau categories; this is a full-area thematic coverage, not a tessellation of reporting units or selected patches.
Polygon regions form a thematic area-wide classification of building/urban style systems, not reporting units or discrete objects; best fits coverage over discrete regions.
Point features mark WWII attack/incidence locations with dates and descriptions, so the layer is mainly an event map of occurrences rather than objects or measurements.

Polygons represent discrete housing development projects/plans rather than a full-area tessellation; the decisive rule is object/project mapping with numeric attributes as counts, not the main phenomenon.

Point features represent individual do-it-yourself plot/project locations, not measurements or events. The decisive rule is point objects with named projects and facility-like attributes, so ObjectDS.
Polygon regions represent area-wide categorical coverage of heritage/suitability classes for solar panels, not reporting units or discrete objects; therefore PlainVectorRegion + CoverageDS.
Point features represent solar panel installations/locations rather than sampled measurements; numeric fields are attributes (detected panels, power) of those objects, so classify as ObjectDS.
Point features marking named swimming locations/facilities; the decisive rule is ObjectDS for distinct real-world places, with PointDS geometry.
